A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LlavaGuard, with matching research aims, taxonomy and dataset lineage. The text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies create localized uncertainties but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original held-out evaluations, LoRA and extreme-rating analyses, and ImageNet and I2P safety audits.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of revised models, additional dataset audits, policy comparisons and a human-agreement study.

M1.justification: The safeguard suite changes from Llava-based 7B/13B/34B models to Llava-OneVision-based 0.5B/7B models. Rationale construction changes from zero-shot generation, filtering and template augmentation to guided generation using prefilled human labels for default policies and category-focused prompts for exceptions (v2 Sections 4–5, Appendix G). The taxonomy and basic policy-exception augmentation remain.

E1.justification: v2 retains the SMID-derived dataset, ImageNet and I2P applications, and adds audits of CC12M, COCO and Stylebreeder (Appendix C, Figure 6). Human evaluation also covers multiple datasets. Its exact synthetic coverage is uncertain: Section 7 lists I2P-generated images, whereas Appendix J lists GenAI-Bench.

E2.justification: v1's Llava-7B/13B/34B, Idefics2-8B and GPT-4 Turbo comparisons are replaced by Llava-OV-0.5B/7B and GPT-4o, with LlamaGuard-3-Vision, OpenAI Omni-Moderation and ImageGuard added (v2 Table 2). v2 also adds Llava as an ImageNet audit comparator. NSFW-1, NSFW-2 and Q16 remain in the appendix comparison.

E3.justification: v2 reports 4571/71/824 train/eval/test samples and 5592 training instances after oversampling. v1 instead describes 4940 training and 599 test samples, although Figure 7 shows 734 test samples. Batching changes to size 1 with 25 accumulation steps. Comparisons introduce precision and PES, and new protocols include ImageGuard policy controls and three human evaluators assessing 105 images each.

E4.justification: v1's full-tuning versus LoRA ablation is removed. The extreme-rating analysis is retained and extended with ambiguous-only results (v2 Table 4). New analyses examine ImageGuard under default versus custom policies, Llava's ImageNet classification errors, and human agreement with ratings, categories and rationales. Qualitative policy-following examples are also revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed information, run-to-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human-agreement study reports point estimates without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v1 Table 3 reports 89.46–90.74% balanced accuracy across its safeguard models; v2 Table 2 reports 88.70% for 0.5B and 90.84% for 7B under revised models and settings, preventing a direct performance-gain interpretation. ImageNet unsafe detections change from 16,640 to approximately 20k, and I2P detections from 996 to approximately 2.2k. New human agreement is 88%, 87% and 81% for ratings, categories and rationales.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition of PES as the harmonic mean of PER and balanced accuracy (Equation 2). Equation 1 explicitly formulates the existing PER metric. No substantial theoretical development, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about flexible policies, explained safety assessments and dataset/model safeguarding remain. v2 explicitly foregrounds an open framework encompassing preprocessing, augmentation and training, and changes the advertised safeguard range from 7–34B to 0.5–7B. These refine the contribution scope while preserving the main research proposition.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for guided rationale generation, attributes ImageGuard's weak policy responsiveness to overfitting, and interprets human agreement as evidence of alignment. It emphasizes handling ambiguous cases and presents smaller checkpoints as addressing computational costs. v1's LoRA-capacity explanation and 13B deployment recommendation disappear; the context dependence of safety and synthetic-rationale limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies concrete guided-generation prompts and prefilled-JSON instructions, expanded dataset accounting, and the human-study procedure and interface. Training documentation changes batching and hardware from four to five A100-80GB GPUs, while retaining three epochs and the learning rate. LoRA and 34B offloading details disappear. Access instructions now point directly to a repository and explicitly include the pipeline.

R1.justification: v2 substantially updates positioning around contemporary visual moderation systems, discussing LlamaGuard-3-Vision, ImageGuard and Omni-Moderation and claiming a distinctive combination of openness and policy flexibility. It adds newer VLM and AIR 2024 references while removing literature associated with the earlier model-selection, LoRA and rationale-generation discussion. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and substantial portions of the background and evaluation narrative are rewritten. v1's Building LlavaGuard section becomes separate Dataset Creation and LlavaGuard Model Suite sections. Appendix organization and terminology are extensively revised, beyond the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one to two columns. Qualitative panels and comparison tables are redesigned, audit charts add dataset-size bars, and new audit, rationale and user-study displays appear. Figures 4–5 retain their example images with rearranged panels; Figure 8 partly redisplays the ImageNet audit alongside a new baseline comparison. The LoRA table disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central promise of reliable, policy-sensitive assessments and explanations. Where v1 supports rationale quality mainly through examples and informal probing, v2 adds component-level human evaluation, explicit competitor policy controls and an ImageNet baseline error analysis, alongside broader real and synthetic dataset validation. Removing the LoRA ablation and retaining reporting inconsistencies, particularly the human-study dataset discrepancy, limit interpretation and reproducibility. Nevertheless, the gains materially strengthen validation of the paper's practical utility.
